title: Hypnosis Guide Emulate Check
intro: This is your hypnosis guide as it is in Git now, with your answers from the last page in, and the strict Emulate check you asked for: every paragraph that isn't yours word for word, compared with your own texts by the check and by fresh readers. Each card has your own version beside it.

Already fixed, because they were plain errors in none of your texts: 31 spaces before a full stop, comma or colon (22 on your last page, 9 more), 53 typos and slips (split words like "day dreams" and "child birth", "a ecology", "yo", "breath" for "breathe", "council" for "counsel", missing question marks, a bracket never closed, "does n’t"), and the references: the book titles in italics again, "(1995) pp", "randomized controlled trials". The list is in fix_typos.py and fix_citations.py in Git.

Click Approve, Reject or Revise on each card, and add a comment if you want. If you leave cards unmarked, tell me whether to take my advice on them as you did last time. Your answers save as you click.

edits.before: I see a lot of connection between reparenting therapy and self hypnosis. They fit well together, though I’d learn to do inner-child therapy sober first, in your ordinary mindstate, since that’s the one you’ll be living in, and get enough Nurturer and Protector in the room before you go deep. When you go into hypnosis the child might come to you. You might see that child in any form. It can be an image, a posture, a voice, a memory, an emotion, etc. It can be any age. It can be any vulnerable part of you. It doesn’t even have to be a “child”, if there is no child there, just work with a protector or whatever you find.

edits.before: If you feel an urge to move, turn, reach, push, or change your body’s position, feel free to either actually do something that will not cause your body pain or discomfort, or just imagine doing what you feel you need to do, and see what happens next. You do not need to “act out” the urge, feel that you need to move, shake, release, etc. If you do move and you feel that you are causing yourself pain or other symptoms that you are concerned about, stop moving.

edits.before: If any “younger” parts come up, offer them the opportunity to spend time with you, or some space if they would rather. All of them are welcome to the “meeting”. You don’t have to get rid of any of them.

edits.before: It is possible that when you try and give the part what it wants, you might feel very upset. It may be that it never got what it needed at the time and now that you are giving it what it wants, it is processing the upset of not getting what it wanted before. If this happens, allow yourself to respond for as long as you want to do so, and for as long as you can ‘stay there’ (ie remain in the process). If you feel that the voice, distance, touch, image etc is too much, then change it to something that is less. Don’t think that you can’t ‘take’ the love.

edits.before: Allow yourself to see where the metaphor takes you. Ask questions like ‘if the problem had an image or story, what would it be?’ or ‘what would need to happen to make things right?’ If it feels like you need to ‘do something’ to give yourself the resource that you feel you need (or to put a boundary in place, or to move away or to take some other action) then try ‘doing that’ for as far as it takes to be of use to you. Remember that whatever you find out is likely to be metaphorical. It may be a good hypothesis for what you need to do but it is not a proven fact.

edits.before: Ending the session. Don’t feel that you have to end the session with a ‘great revelation’! When you have done as much as you want to do, it is a good idea to find out if there is anything that you need to do to make sure that you can leave things where they are for the time being. This might include thanking parts for their help, or making sure that you do something ‘in real life’ (eat a good meal, put a boundary in place, get some rest, repair a relationship, keep a promise etc). Whatever it is, tell your little one, "That’s enough for today. We’re going back to the life we’re building."

You don’t need to write down the whole cast of characters, just what you actually noticed.

edits.before: If the fake feeling is telling you that you don't have the 'grown up' ability to do this yet, then don't try and convince yourself by using an inner voice. As long as you can still observe yourself well enough to do this, try and borrow what you need from someone who you can imagine is 'good enough' to lend it to you. This could be a family member, friend, famous person etc. What you need might be warmth, boundary, direction etc. For warmth, just make sure it's someone who liked you the way you were. suggestions.title: Who wrote the ISH article

edits.before: Healing the Divided Self, Maggie Phillips and Claire Frederick (1995), pp 24-27, 45-50, 83-90, covers a lot of aspects of this post, such as interactive hypnosis, helping the subject learn how to learn by using other senses, learning self hypnosis, making sure the subject comes back at the end, etc. However, this is a professional clinical book, not a self help book, so be careful about trying to use the procedures used with the cases, etc in this book for solo work (the same applies to historical information it contains). Also, Adam Eason's work with Benjamin Parris in the International Society of Hypnosis, specifically his article about self hypnosis, should be a useful thing to read (especially the parts that talk about how to learn to learn when you're directing it yourself, and about whether you need another person to help you, and using recordings to help you, etc.)

suggestions.title: What chapter 7 is about, and what the links back up

edits.before: Chapter 7 of Trauma and Memory, by Peter Levine, 2015, contains useful information on this. This US Veterans Administration website contains useful general information about hypnosis, such as the fact that it can be very strong and should be carefully used, and that it may result in false memories. This ASCH website contains information about the usefulness of getting certified in hypnosis, and why it doesn't guarantee competence. Links are available for these and other useful groups in the evidence and specialist sections, but they point to their particular claims, not every use of hypnosis.
